title: security: enforce RBAC v2 KMS region pinning and tighten audit logging for data residency
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Enforce RBAC v2 KMS region pinning for resource-level key residency; enhance audit logging to include KMS key residency metadata and policy decision context; provide a migration tool to backfill existing resources and surface non-compliant keys.
description:
Context: customers in regulated industries require stronger guarantees that customer-managed keys (CMKs) and KMS usage respect data residency policies. Previous RBAC v2 rules allowed KMS keys to be used across regions when a higher-level policy existed, which created gaps in audits and compliance reports. This PR hardens the RBAC v2 enforcement path to fail-fast on cross-region KMS usage unless an explicit residency exception is present.

What this change does: - Add enforcement step in RBAC v2 evaluator to validate KMS key region against resource residency (region pinning). Enforcement is configurable as 'audit' (log only) or 'enforce' (deny). - Emit structured audit events that include: policy_id, decision (allow/deny/audit), kms_key_arn, kms_key_region, resource_region, principal, request_id, and policy_evaluation_trace. These events are indexed by the audit pipeline. - Provide a migration/backfill subcommand (rbacctl residency backfill) that scans existing resources and emits remediation suggestions and a report. - Add unit and integration tests for evaluator changes and add an end-to-end test that exercises a policy with residency constraints against a cross-region KMS key.

Motivation: closes compliance gaps reported by SUP-8842 and reduces manual work for security teams when verifying KMS residency. The enforcement path will be rolled out behind a feature flag and released as 'audit' by default for 2 weeks before flipping to 'enforce' for customers with the flag enabled.

Notes: - This PR intentionally keeps default behavior non-breaking (audit mode) and ships a migration tool before aggressive enforcement. - Customers can opt into enforcement via account settings or via a Linear workflow for enterprise contracts.

Testing: automated unit tests, integration tests in perf-canary, and a staged canary rollout to dedicated clusters.

Related: ENG-4321, ENG-4410, SUP-8842. See also docs update in redwood-docs (follow-up PR) for control plane UI and CLI usage.
